most_likely: Desmoid tumor (aggressive fibromatosis) of anterior abdominal wall, neoplasm of uncertain behavior of soft tissue, status post cryoablation
summary: Middle-aged woman with a large painful right anterior abdominal wall desmoid tumor (biopsy-proven, previously 14 cm) admitted overnight after staged CT/ultrasound-guided cryoablation of the residual tumor. The procedure was uncomplicated; she was observed for post-procedural right-sided abdominal/flank pain and transient nausea, managed with dilaudid PCA, IV ketorolac and IV ondansetron, then transitioned to oral agents. Labs show a reactive post-ablation leukocytosis (WBC 12.5 → 15.2) and thrombocytosis without evidence of infection or bleeding; chronic hepatitis C (genotype 3, VL ~430,000) was unchanged inpatient.
